transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I keep avoiding my workshop, and family get-togethers if my brother-in-law might be there. I’ve been planning around those reminders for so long, and I’m tired of it.
Can you tell me if something specific happened involving your brother-in-law that made you start avoiding him and the workshop?

I just started keeping away from him, and from my workshop too. Family gatherings if I think he’ll be there—I don’t go. I’ve spent a long time arranging things so I won’t run into those reminders, and I’m tired of living that way.
When you say he and the workshop are 'reminders,' can you tell me what they remind you of—was there a specific distressing or traumatic event involving him or that place?
It’s his hand, really—holding that heavy tool. It comes back like a picture in my head out of nowhere, when I’m shaving or working on a painting. My chest still tightens up when I see it.
How long ago did you first start avoiding the workshop and your brother-in-law, and how long has this pattern been going on?
It started after that confrontation with my brother-in-law—about two years and four months ago. It’s been going on ever since.
During that confrontation with your brother-in-law, did you feel your life was in danger or that you might be seriously hurt?
I’m not sure how to put that. I remember being very upset, but I can’t really say more about whether I thought my life was in danger.

Besides these intrusive images and chest tightness, have you also been having nightmares about that day, or noticed feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping since it happened?
Most nights I get to bed all right, but I lie there listening for noises in the house. Sometimes I wake up from a bad dream about the workshop, and then I’m wide awake for an hour or two.
Can you describe what actually happened during that confrontation—did your brother-in-law physically threaten you or raise that tool against you in a way that made you fear being hurt?
I—I don’t really know. I remember being upset and the whole thing felt bad, but I can’t clearly say whether he threatened me physically or whether I thought I was going to be hurt.
Since that confrontation, have you noticed feeling emotionally numb or distant from people, or having persistent negative thoughts about yourself or the world that weren't there before?

I’ve been thinking differently about people, I guess. I used to feel like family was where you could let your guard down. Now I catch myself thinking you can’t really trust anybody, even the people sitting at your own table.
During that confrontation, did your brother-in-law actually strike you, injure you, or cause any physical harm?
I can’t say for sure. I remember being frightened and upset, but I don’t clearly remember whether he actually hit me or hurt me physically.
At the moment the confrontation was happening, did you feel an overwhelming sense of fear, horror, or helplessness, even if you can't say for certain whether you were in physical danger?
I’m not sure I’d call it overwhelming fear or horror. I was upset and shaken, certainly, but I can’t clearly say I felt helpless or that I thought something terrible was about to happen.
Can you tell me whether your brother-in-law actually raised or swung that tool toward your body during the confrontation, in a way that could have caused you physical injury?
I honestly can’t say. It’s all a bit unclear to me—I don’t remember seeing him raise or swing it toward me specifically.
Aside from the tool, do you recall any physical contact during the confrontation—such as being pushed, grabbed, or restrained by your brother-in-law?
I don’t really remember any physical contact. I can’t say he pushed me or grabbed me—it's just not clear in my mind.

Setting aside what you remember about physical contact, can you tell me what the confrontation was actually about—was it mainly a heated argument or verbal conflict, or was there something else that made you feel your safety was at risk?
I’m not really sure. I remember it as an argument, more verbal than anything, but the details are hazy. I can’t point to anything specific that made me think my safety was at risk.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports significant avoidance behavior (avoiding his workshop and family gatherings), intrusive imagery, hyperarousal (hypervigilance, disrupted sleep), and altered cognitions about trust, all emerging after an identifiable psychosocial stressor (a verbal confrontation with his brother-in-law). However, repeated and specific questioning failed to establish that the stressor met Criterion A for PTSD (actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, or subjective sense of life-threat/helplessness/horror at the time). The patient explicitly denied certainty about physical threat, injury, or overwhelming fear/helplessness at the time of the event, and described it primarily as a verbal argument. Given a clear identifiable stressor with resulting emotional and behavioral disturbance (avoidance, distress, hypervigilance, negative interpersonal cognitions) causing functional impairment, but insufficient severity/nature of the stressor to meet PTSD criteria, Adjustment Disorder (F43.2) is the most fitting diagnosis. The chronicity (2 years 4 months) is longer than typical adjustment disorder but is still better explained by an adjustment reaction with prolonged/persistent stressor-related avoidance than by PTSD, given the unmet Criterion A threshold.
